title: Interactive Subnet Debugger & Packet-Path Replay
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Operators and tenant support engineers lack a lightweight interactive tool in the Private console to trace how a single request traversed subnets, egress points, and tenant network policies during an incident or upgrade. Current troubleshooting requires jumping between logs, topology maps, and cloud consoles. This ticket proposes an in-console Subnet Debugger with a packet-path replay mode: a time-travel UI that overlays a single request's path across subnets, NAT/egress gateways, and ACLs with annotated latency and drop points.

Goal: Ship a design prototype and interaction spec that can be implemented by the networking team and integrated with our audit/logging pipeline. The prototype should enable: 1) selecting a request (by trace id or time range), 2) visualizing it as a timeline + compact network strip, 3) replaying packet hops with playback controls, and 4) surfacing suggested remediation actions (restart, route-swap, open CCR) with deep links to the workflows.

Scope & constraints: UI-only prototype and interaction spec (Figma + interaction notes). Backend integration (log ingestion, trace linking) will be handled in a follow-up ENG ticket. Must respect tenant isolation: no cross-tenant visibility beyond what current audit logs allow. Must not expose payload contents.

Success metrics: prototype validated in two internal support playtests (time-to-detect reduced by 30%), design approved by ENG and PM, and handoff artifacts that allow ENG to scope ETA and dependencies.
design_goals: Single-request centric view: unify timeline + network strip
Compact mode for on-call quick glance and expanded mode for deep analysis
Actionable remediation anchors (link to runbooks/ops actions)
Respect tenant isolation and PII-by-default rules
acceptance_criteria: Figma prototype with three states: compact summary, expanded timeline, and packet replay
Interaction spec describing keyboard controls, playback speeds, and error-step hopping
Design handoff doc listing required logs/fields for ENG (trace id, hop timestamps, latency, egress node id, policy evaluation result)
Two asynchronous internal playtests recorded with annotated findings
PM and Lead Engineer sign-off on feasibility and security constraints
decisions: Use an inline horizontal 'network strip' visualization instead of full node graph to reduce visual complexity
Playback will be event-driven (based on timestamps) rather than packet-level micro-simulation to limit backend requirements
Remediation anchors will be deep links that open the existing ops command palette, not execute actions directly from the debugger
Expose only metadata (node ids, policy decision outcomes, latencies) — never show request body or headers
tradeoffs: Compact strip vs full graph: we sacrifice topological completeness for quick readability on-call
Playback fidelity vs backend load: coarser time granularity reduces required ingestion effort but can mask microbursts
Actionability vs safety: we prefer deep-links to manual actions to avoid creating new high-risk controls in the console
